page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-192 is an x86_64 server instance provisioned with 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware architecture features 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration via AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Total system memory measures 1488 GB, yielding an allocation of 7.75 GB per vCPU. The instance configuration includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution capacity for multi-threaded and memory-bound workloads. In stress-ng evaluations, multi-core throughput reaches the top 10 percent with a score of 165331.17, contrasted with single-core performance that settles in the middle 50 percent tier at 2096.79. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 573.67 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 246.84 GB/sec for write operations. Software compilation tests with Clang and PassMark CPU metrics also achieve top-tier classifications, while in-memory throughput tests yield 209.65 million Redis SET operations per second.

The high density of processor cores and RAM provides qualitative cost efficiency for organizations looking to consolidate large, multi-socket scale workloads into a single virtual machine rather than managing distributed nodes. Primary tradeoffs involve the reliance on network storage due to the absence of integrated local NVMe disks, alongside modest single-thread processor speeds. Best-fit enterprise workloads include high-capacity in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching clusters, multi-threaded build farms, and batch data processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-192 is an x86_64 compute instance configured with 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 96 physical cores powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 1488 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB per vCPU, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache and support for AMX and AVX-512 instructions. The instance incorporates no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote volumes for persistence. Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional multi-threaded performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics ranking in the top decile, paired with large-block memory read bandwidth of 573.67 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics operate near the median. The dense hardware profile provides high compute and memory consolidation, avoiding multi-node clustering overhead for memory-heavy operations. Appropriate workloads include high-capacity in-memory databases like Redis, extensive data warehousing and ETL pipelines, multi-threaded software compilation, and large CPU-based matrix operations.
